comments.note: FakeBootstrapper.CheckAsync throws synchronously (not via a faulted Task) when throws: true. All test callers use try/catch around await, so this works correctly in practice. However, for strict async-interface fidelity the throw could be wrapped: return Task.FromException<DatabaseBootstrapResult>(new InvalidOperationException(...)). Low-risk follow-up if desired.

Inline private fakes still present in ViewLocatorTests.cs, PasswordSetupViewModelTests.cs, and MainWindowViewModelTests.cs. These shadow the shared TestHelpers/ variants but compile and test cleanly. Removal is deferred per the Developer's handoff note — a subsequent WP should migrate callers to the shared fakes.

summary: All four shared fakes in TestHelpers/ reviewed against their production interfaces. No blocking issues found.
FakeBootstrapper: constructor-param design (result + throws) correctly unifies fixed-result and throwing variants. IDatabaseBootstrapper interface fully satisfied.
FakeExternalToolProvisioner: takes caller-supplied Exception? — more flexible than the bool-flag pattern used in the other three fakes. Interface fully satisfied.
FakePasswordService: mutable-property design is well-suited for stateful per-test configuration; all three IPasswordService methods correctly implemented.

FakeDatabaseConnectionStore: most complex fake; correctly implements auto-Guid assignment per IDatabaseConnectionStore.SaveAsync spec, and correctly clears ActiveId on DeleteAsync. Full CRUD semantics faithfully replicated.

comments.note: Exception-injection API is inconsistent across the four fakes: FakeExternalToolProvisioner accepts a caller-supplied Exception? (flexible, allows custom message and type), while FakeBootstrapper, FakePasswordService, and FakeDatabaseConnectionStore use bool flags and hardcode InvalidOperationException internally. The FakeExternalToolProvisioner pattern is more reusable. If the follow-up WP extends the shared fakes, consider normalising to the Exception? pattern.

MainWindowViewModelTests retains an inline FakeBootstrapper that uses a mutable StatusToReturn property — a different API surface from TestHelpers.FakeBootstrapper (which takes constructor params). The two are not drop-in compatible. The follow-up WP that migrates inline fakes to shared fakes will need to either (a) extend TestHelpers.FakeBootstrapper with a mutable property, or (b) rewrite the affected tests to use the constructor-param approach. Surfacing early to avoid a surprise during migration.

MainWindowViewModelTests also contains an inline FakeThemeService (IThemeService) that has no shared equivalent in TestHelpers/. The follow-up migration WP should either add FakeThemeService to TestHelpers/ or explicitly exclude it from scope.

[documentation-forward] FakeBootstrapper default result uses revision value 35. The XML doc states 'Defaults to (Ok, 35)' but does not explain that 35 is an arbitrary non-zero test value with no business meaning. Add a brief inline comment or extend the param doc to clarify this for future contributors.
